newsitem.title: NIGER: Massive arrests in Niger after arms find-officials.
newsitem.headline: Massive arrests in Niger after arms find-officials.

text.p: Security forces are pursuing large-scale arrests in Niger following the seizure of a large cache of ammunition and grenades in the capital Niamey, interior ministry officials said on Monday
The identity of those held in the crackdown, which started on Saturday, has not been disclosed.
State radio said security forces seized 30,000 rounds of ammunition and an unspecified number of grenades on Friday night.

Interior Minister IdI Ango immediately called on security forces to be extra vigilant in maintaining order in the impoverished West African country riven by political tension since a military coup last January.
"For the sake of public order and peace, the government will rise to its responsibilities, whatever the threat," Ango said on television on Sunday.

Opposition leaders who have clashed with authorities in their campaign against the election of coupmaker General Ibrahim Bare Mainassara dismissed an earlier announcement of an arms find as a smokescreen to crack down on them.
Mainassara seized power, saying he wanted to end a showdown between the elected president and the prime minister that was paralysing the government of the impoverished country.
He called early elections following Western pressure. But he pushed through a constitution giving greater powers to the president, before standing for the post himself. On the
second day of voting in the May 7-8 election, Mainassara put all his four rivals under house arrest, freeing them on July 22. A handpicked electoral commission declared him elected.
State radio said Friday's seizure followed a government order for "drastic" checks after the discovery of arms at Madaoua, 500 km (315 miles) east of Niamey a week ago.
The government described arms seized there as "extremely sophisticated material meant for attacks and acts of destruction" and ordered strict controls at borders, airports, and highways.
